text = frontmatter + """ CHAPTER V

NAMES OF ALL PRĀYAŚCITTAS

[[P130]]Now all the [[prāyascittas|prāyaścittas]] mentioned in the [[smrtis|smṛtis]] and digests will be arranged in alphabetical order (Sanskrit, transliterated into English), excepting mere hymns, fasts, &c. and brief explanations and references will be added to each.

[[AGHAMARSANA-( The|AGHAMARṢAṆA—(The]] hymn [[Rg.|Ṛg.]] X.190.1–3).

item.title: 01 Pātaka
item.description:
[[CHAPTER I|SECTION I]]

PĀTAKA, [[PRĀYAŚCITTA AND KARMAVIPAKA.|PRĀYAŚCITTA AND KARMAVIPĀKA.]]

(Sins, expiations and the residual consequences of sins).

CHAPTER I

[[P1]][[20 The|The]] Article on sin in Hasting’s Encyclopædia of Religion and Ethics (vol. 11) will clearly show how the idea of sin varies from religion to religion, from age to age and from [[coun try|country]] to country. We are concerned here with the growth and [[developinent|development]] of the doctrine of sin in India from Vedic times to the medieval digests and commentaries on [[Dharmaśāstra, do|Dharmaśāstra.]]

item.title: 02 Means of Reducing Consequences of Sins
item.description:
CHAPTER II

MEANS OF REDUCING CONSEQUENCES OF SINS

[[P41]]Confession—In [[Ap.|Āp.]] [[Dh,|Dh.]] S. [[1.|I.]] 9. 24. 15, [[1.|I.]] 10. [[28, 19,|28. 19,]] [[1. 10.29.1|I. 10. 29. 1]] it is prescribed that the person undergoing a penance for being an abhiśasta or for unjustly forsaking his wife or for the murder of a learned brāhmaṇa has to declare his misdeed while begging for alms to support himself. The Vedic student who was guilty of sexual intercourse had also to proclaim his lapse while begging at seven houses ([[Gaut,|Gaut.]] 23.18, Manu XI. [[122 ).|122).]]1

item.title: 03 Prayaścitta
item.description:
CHAPTER III

PRĀYAŚCITTA; ITS ORIGIN, DERIVATION AND MEANING

[[P57]]It is now necessary to turn to prāyaścittas as removers of sin. A number of subjects will fall to be treated [[here,|here.]]

First, an attempt must be made to understand the [[etymo logy|etymology]] and meaning of the word [[‘prāyascitta’|‘prāyaścitta’]] in ancient times. There are two forms of the word, prāyaścitti and prāyaścitta, which occur in Vedic works without distinction of meaning and both forms are fairly old, though prāyaścitti appears to be the older of the two. The form [[prāyascitti|prāyaścitti]] frequently occurs in the [[Tai, S.|Tai. S.]] (as in [[II, 1.2,4,|II. 1.2.4,]] [[II. 1 4.1,|II. 1.4.1,]] [[III. 1,3,2-3,|III. 1.3.2-3,]] V. 1.9.3, V. 3.12.1)1. In some of these passages no question of sin arises. The word means ‘doing [[some thing|something]] which would get rid of some accidental happening or mishap such as the breaking of an [[ukha|ukhā]] (a pot or saucepan for boiling or cooking) or the sun’s losing its [[brilliance,’|brilliance.’]] In Tai. S. V. 3.12.1 the word is used in the sense of an expiation for a sin. So even in very old books the word had two shades of meaning. The [[Kausitaki|Kauṣītaki]]2 Br. [[(vi, 12)|(VI. 12)]] states : [[““they|“they]] say ‘whatever mistake or excess occurs in the sacrifice that affects the priest brahmā, that he treats with the [[three fold|three-fold]] learning (i. e. the three Vedas)”. The word also occurs in the Atharvaveda XIV. 1.30, Vāj. S. 39.12 (in close proximity to [[niskrti),|niṣkṛti),]] in the Ait. Br. V. 27, in the [[Sat. Br.|Śat. Br.]] [[IV.5.7.1,|IV. 5. 7.1,]] VII. 1.4.9, XI. 5.3.8, XII. 4.1.6 and in other works also. The form prāyaścitta occurs in [[Kausitaki|Kauṣītaki]] Br. V. 9, [[VI 12|VI. 12]] and elsewhere. The Āśv. Śr. III. 10.38 and [[śānkhāyana|Śāṅkhāyana]] Śr. III. 19.1 respectively employ the words [[prāyascitti|prāyaścitti]] and prāyaścitta3. In Pār. [[gr.|gṛ.]] I. [[P58]]10 the form ‘prāyaścitti’ is employed. Jai. in several places [[* employs|employs]] the word prāyaścitta (as in VI. 3.7, VI. 4.10, VI 5.45 and 49, XII. 3.16). [[Sabara|Śabara]]4 on the last sūtra [[(XII, 3.16)|(XII. 3.16)]] [[ex plains|explains]] that the prāyaścittas (in the [[Sruti|Śruti]] texts) are of two kinds, viz. some are meant to make good the defect in the procedure and materials of sacrifice which arises or befalls through some neglect or heedlessness, while others are subsidiary parts of a rite when an occasion arises i. e. they are undertaken to atone for not doing what is ordained or doing something which is forbidden (e. g. non-performance of daily Agnihotra even though the sun rises). The [[Sat. Br.|Śat. Br.]]5 XII. 4 and Ait. Br. 32.2-11 [[pro vide|provide]] some interesting and amusing examples of the mishaps for which [[prāyascittas|prāyaścittas]] are provided e. g. when a vicious boar, ram or dog runs between the [[sacrifical|sacrificial]] fires, or if Agnihotra milk gets spilled while the cow is being milked or if the milk pot is turned upside down or if it were to [[break,|break]] or if the cow were to lie down while being milked, or if the fire were to go out after the first libation is offered etc. Vide also [[Mānava-gphya|Mānava-gṛhya]] I. 3, Hir. [[gr.|gṛ.]] [[I.-5.1-16,|I. 5.1-16,]] Bhāradvāja [[gr.|gṛ.]] II. 32, [[Kausika-sūtra|Kauśika-sūtra]] 46. 14-55, [[Aģv. Sr.|Āśv. Śr.]] III. 10 and [[Asv. gr.|Āśv. gṛ.]] III. 6-7 for similar occurrences and prāyaścittas. The [[Mahābhāsya|Mahābhāṣya]] on Pāṇ. VI. 1.157 [[explains111|explains]]6 both [[prāyascitti|prāyaścitti]] and prāyaścitta on the analogy of the word Pāraskara. [[Prāyascittas|Prāyaścittas]] may be said to be, in the language of the [[Mimāmsā,|Mīmāṁsā,]] either kratvartha or puruṣārtha. The former are prescribed in the [[Srautasūtras.|Śrautasūtras.]] It is the latter kind of [[prāya scittas|prāyaścittas]] that are generally dealt with in [[Smrti|Smṛti]] works on [[prāya Ścitta.|prāyaścitta.]] In this work the prāyaścittas mentioned in [[Srauta|Śrauta]] [[P59]]works are passed over, as they have either been mentioned in vol. II. or were of rare occurrence even in olden days.

item.title: 04 Penances for Particular Sins
item.description:
CHAPTER IV

PENANCES FOR PARTICULAR SINS

[[P87]]It is now proper to turn to the penances prescribed for individual sins of different types (grave sins, minor sins and the like). It may be noted that the [[smrtis|smṛtis]] contain numerous prāyaścittas for the same sin and that it is often difficult to reconcile all the dicta. The commentaries and digests such as the [[Mit,|Mit.]] and the Prāyaścitta-viveka therefore try to assign to each penance an appropriate provision, looking to all the [[circum stances|circumstances]] noted above (i.e. they are bent on [[‘visayavyavasthā’).206a|‘viṣayavyavasthā’).1]] In this work, it is not necessary to set out in detail the numerous penances for numberless lapses that are prescribed in the several [[smrtis|smṛtis]] and digests. In the [[Sabdakalpadruma|Śabdakalpadruma]] (part III) there is an analysis from the Prāyaścitta-viveka alone of the several lapses, the penances for them, the number of cows to be donated as substitutes, the monetary equivalents when even cows cannot be donated and the [[daksinā|dakṣiṇā]] in each case, which occupy pages 321 to 364. Setting out all these lapses together with the penances for them would only be a matter of academic interest and of no practical value, as almost all the [[prāyaścittag|prāyaścittas]] have become antiquated and are hardly ever performed now except in the form of gifts of cows or money to [[brāhmanas,|brāhmaṇas,]] pilgrimages and recitation of Vedic mantras or japa of the names of some favourite deity such as [[Visnu|Viṣṇu]] or [[Siva.|Śiva.]] Therefore only a few typical sins alone will be taken for treatment here and later on a list of all penances with brief descriptions will be [[furnished|furnished.]]

item.title: 06 Consequences of Not Undergoing Penances
item.description:
CHAPTER VI

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT UNDERGOING PENANCES

[[P153]]If a sinner did not undergo a prāyaścitta, the [[Smộtis,|Smṛtis,]] [[Purānas,|Purāṇas,]] medieval digests declared that he had to suffer dire and far-reaching consequences. Yāj. III. 221 declares that men addicted to sins, who feel no repentance and who [[(therefore )|(therefore)]] do not undergo the proper penances, fall into painful and [[horri ble|horrible]] hells. Manu [[XIT.|XII.]] 54 ff and [[Yaj. III,|Yāj. III.]] 206 ff provide that those guilty of grave (and other) sins after having passed numbers of years in hells and suffered the tortures of horrible hells are born again in this world because of (the remnants of their) evil actions in different forms such as lower animals, insects, trees and shrubs &c. Manu XI. 53 ordains that one should always perform penance in order to free oneself from sins, since those who have not destroyed their sins (by means of prāyaścittas) are born again endowed with disgraceful marks (such as having bad nails, black teeth &c.). Manu XI. 48 also emphasizes that wicked men suffer mal-formations owing to their wicked deeds committed in this very life or in a former life. The [[Vispu purāṇa 355|Viṣṇupurāṇa]]1 echoes the words of Yāj. III. 221. The [[Visnudharmo ttara|Viṣṇudharmottara]] [[declares 356|declares]]2 that those [[(sinners )|(sinners)]] who do not undergo penances nor are punished by the king fall into hell and are born also as lower animals and even after attaining human bodies they become marked (with bodily defects). [[Viṣnu|Viṣṇu]] Dh. S. [[(44, 1-10)|(44. 1–10)]] [[prescribes 357|prescribes]]3 that evil-doers, having experienced the horrors of hell pass into animal bodies and that those guilty of atipātakas, mahāpātakas, anupātakas, upapātakas, [[jāti|jāti-]] [[P154]][[bhramsa-kara|bhraṁśa-kara]] actions, [[sankarikarana,|saṅkarīkaraṇa,]] [[apatrikarana,|apātrīkaraṇa,]] [[nialini karana|malinīkaraṇa]] and miscellaneous sins, respectively enter the bodies of all plants, of worms (or insects), of birds, of aquatic animals, of animals roving in waters, of deer, of cattle, of untouchables among men, of miscellaneous and cruel carnivorous animals (like tigers). [[Visnu Dh, S. 45.1|Viṣṇu Dh. S. 45.1]] [[provides 358|provides]]4 that sinners, after having undergone the horrors of hells and after having passed through the bodies of lower animals, are born as human beings with certain marks (indicative of their sins). So the teaching of these and other authorities comes to this that sins when not expiated by penances or by State punishment, lead to hell, that then, owing to some remnants of the evil deeds, to birth as lower animals and then as decrepit or diseased human beings.
